long_biography.plain_text:
Before becoming Clayton's chief executive, Kevin Clayton spent time outside his father's homebuilding company and earned an MBA at the University of Tennessee. Back at Clayton, he managed its south-eastern region, then led the finance, building and retail operations in turn. Those assignments prepared him to succeed Jim Clayton at the head of the business in 1999.

Berkshire Hathaway bought Clayton in 2003, with Kevin remaining chief executive. He steered the former manufactured-housing specialist into site-built homebuilding through acquisitions of regional builders, while its factory-built lines continued to develop. Clayton's CrossMod homes add permanent foundations and features associated with conventional houses to an off-site construction process.
